Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. ## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the disciples are numbered and named in later works, with their occupations and their travels.
- Hadith to add later: reports about the disciples of Isa, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Isa calls for helpers  (`#isa-calls-for-helpers`)

Cited ayat: 3:52-53

> **3:52** فَلَمَّآ أَحَسَّ عِيسَىٰ مِنْهُمُ ٱلْكُفْرَ قَالَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ
>
> **3:53** رَبَّنَآ ءَامَنَّا بِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ وَٱتَّبَعْنَا ٱلرَّسُولَ فَٱكْتُبْنَا مَعَ ٱلشَّٰهِدِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (3:52): When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God.

**c2** (3:52): The disciples said that they were God's helpers, that they believed in God, and asked him to bear witness that they submit.

**c3** (3:53): They said, our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and have followed the messenger, so write us down among the witnesses.

### One-minute summary

When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers and that they believed in God [c2]. They prayed to be written down among the witnesses [c3].

### Complete story

When Isa sensed disbelief from them, he asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers, that they believed in God, and asked him to bear witness that they submit [c2]. They said, our Lord, we believe in what You sent down and have followed the messenger, so write us down among the witnesses [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah gives the disciples' answer in parts, an address to Isa and a prayer to their Lord [c2][c3]. The word for submit, muslimun, is rendered by its general sense here [c2].

### Kids mode

Isa asked who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers [c2]. They prayed to be written down among the witnesses [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the disciples answer a call for help with a statement of belief and a prayer [c2][c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who they were, how many, or where this took place.
- Not established: from whom Isa sensed disbelief, beyond the word them.
- Not established: what the word hawariyyun means in its origin; the ayat use it without explaining it.

## 2. The inspiration to the disciples  (`#the-inspiration-to-the-disciples`)

Cited ayat: 5:111

> **5:111** وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى ٱلْحَوَارِيِّـۧنَ أَنْ ءَامِنُوا۟ بِى وَبِرَسُولِى قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَٱشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنَا مُسْلِمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (5:111): God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger, and that they said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit.

### One-minute summary

God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger [c1]. They said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit [c1].

### Complete story

God says that He inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger, and that they said that they believed and asked Him to bear witness that they submit [c1].

### Deep study

The ayah speaks of an inspiration to the disciples, and the verb is the one used for inspiration generally [c1]. It does not say how the inspiration came [c1].

### Kids mode

God inspired the disciples to believe in Him and in His messenger [c1]. They said that they believed [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah presents the disciples' belief as something God inspired [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how the inspiration came to them.
- Not established in this ayah: who the messenger is; the ayah does not name him.

## 3. Believers and disbelievers  (`#believers-and-disbelievers`)

Cited ayat: 61:14

> **61:14** يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوٓا۟ أَنصَارَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّـۧنَ مَنْ أَنصَارِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ قَالَ ٱلْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ ٱللَّهِ فَـَٔامَنَت طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنۢ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ وَكَفَرَت طَّآئِفَةٌ فَأَيَّدْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ عَلَىٰ عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ ظَٰهِرِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (61:14): God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples, who are my helpers toward God, and the disciples said that they were God's helpers.

**c2** (61:14): One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group disbelieved, and God supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became prevailing.

### One-minute summary

God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another disbelieved [c2]. God supported those who believed against their enemy [c2].

### Complete story

God tells the believers to be helpers of God, as Isa, son of Maryam, said to the disciples, who are my helpers toward God, and the disciples said that they were God's helpers [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group disbelieved, and God supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became prevailing [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah recalls the call of Isa as an example for the believers [c1]. The Arabic word rendered prevailing can also mean uppermost or manifest, and the ayah does not say in what way they prevailed [c2].

### Kids mode

Isa, son of Maryam, asked the disciples who would be his helpers toward God [c1]. The disciples said that they were God's helpers [c1]. One group of the Children of Israel believed and another group did not [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah asks the believers to answer as the disciples answered [c1]. Another is that it ends by recording that God supported those who believed [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who the enemy was, or when this support came.
- Not established: in what way those who believed prevailed.
- Not established: the numbers in the groups, or how they divided.
